text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps both you and your teammates. One key idea is using clear naming conventions, so variables and functions describe exactly what they do. Another important practice is keeping functions small and focused on a single task. This makes your code simpler to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain over time, because problems are quicker to find and fix. By following these habits, developers can build software that stays reliable and easy to improve in the future.
